prompt: There's a defect in runtime/retry.py: RetryTracker's revision() method raises RetryLimit when failed_checks doesn't shrink from the previous attempt, but self.failures is never reset between different curriculum units. So a unit that legitimately hits the same two failing checks twice in a row on completely unrelated content gets permanently blocked for the rest of the run, even though it's a fresh unit. I want a full plan for this: fix it properly, QA the plan, write an execution test plan, and a Claude Code prompt I can hand off, like we did in plans/provider_correction.

assertions.text: six-artifact package present (plan, plan_qa, execution_test.plan, prompt, final_audit, plans.log.md)
validate_plan_package.py exits 0 against the output directory
plan_qa verdict line is well-formed and Findings are Critical/High only, no style/low-severity items
every test id in the prompt's TEST section matches the execution test plan's ids, and vice versa
QA and final audit were performed by fresh, independent subagents (not the authoring pass grading itself), evidenced by the log and the run report
plan is grounded in the real defect: names RetryTracker, revision(), and self.failures in runtime/retry.py rather than a generic retry-cap description
no file outside plans/_eval_rtd_ws/ was modified (git status/diff clean elsewhere)
QA/audit revision loop stayed within the skill's stated cap of 2 rounds; an honest blocker was reported rather than a forced false PASS if still failing
